facts.text: Turkish red pine has very thick bark. Thanks to it, fires that burn along the ground hurt the tree only a little.
If you see even the smallest smoke in a forest or field, stay away and call 112 right away. Even a tiny bit of smoke is worth reporting!
Around the Mediterranean, summer can last from June to October. In these long summers there is almost no rain!
Fire usually moves faster uphill than downhill or on flat ground. So it can climb a mountain very quickly!
Wind brings fresh oxygen to a fire and pushes it toward new plants. That is why wind is one of the most important things in a fire.
Clouds, thick smoke or treetops can hide a fire from a satellite completely. If a satellite did not see a fire, that does not mean there is none!
A fire can start and end before a satellite looks again. That is why satellites never see some fires.
Some fires are too small or not hot enough for a satellite to notice. A satellite may miss them!
A hot spot seen by a satellite is not always a forest fire. Sometimes it is a volcano or the flame of a gas well!
Satellite data reaches NASA's fire map within 3 hours of the satellite looking. So what you see on the map may be a few hours old!
NASA's Aqua satellite goes around the Earth in about 99 minutes. One whole trip in the time of a movie!
When the weather is hot, dry and windy, fires start, grow and spread more easily.
Embers from a fire can fly for miles and start new fires. Even if a fire looks far away, listen to the warnings from officials!
Even sparks from harvesting machines can lead to forest fires at harvest time. That is why looking after those machines matters so much.
Smoke from burning field stalks can make it hard to see on the road. It can even cause traffic accidents!
facts.source_name: Şanlıurfa Provincial Directorate of Agriculture and Forestry
